era: PlayStation / Arcade / Dreamcast / Neo Geo Pocket Color / PlayStation 2
summary: UEP Systems and Sony's snowboarding series; use the newest official rerelease for the original, PS1/Dreamcast emulation for the classic sequels, and PS2 for the later higher-fidelity entries.

entries.title: Cool Boarders

emulation.notes: Use the official release first; DuckStation is the local-preservation fallback.
emulation.fidelity_ceiling: Official modern emulation or high-resolution PS1 emulation

primary.version: Nintendo Switch 2 / PlayStation 5 Console Archives release
primary.why: The original PlayStation game has official PS one Classic, PS4/PS5, and Console Archives re-releases; the 2026 Console Archives route is the newest sourced official preservation path.
primary.how_to_play: Play the Console Archives release on Nintendo Switch 2 or PlayStation 5; use DuckStation with the original PlayStation disc/image only for comparison.

entries.remaster_caveats: Official emulated rerelease, not a remake.

entries.title: Cool Boarders 2

emulation.notes: Use NTSC original where possible; compare PSN only if already owned.

primary.why: Cool Boarders 2 is a PlayStation game with PSN and PlayStation Classic re-release routes, but the original PS1 release under high-resolution emulation avoids the PAL-version caveat documented for the PlayStation Classic lineup.
primary.how_to_play: Play the original PlayStation release on DuckStation with internal-resolution scaling; use PSN if already owned.

entries.remaster_caveats: PSN/PlayStation Classic are emulated re-releases, not remasters.

entries.title: Cool Boarders Arcade Jam

emulation.notes: Use original arcade hardware where possible.

primary.why: Cool Boarders Arcade Jam is a 1998 main-series arcade game; no home port is known.
primary.how_to_play: Play on original arcade hardware or an accurate arcade preservation setup if available.

entries.remaster_caveats: No home port or modern remaster exists.

emulation.notes: Use internal-resolution scaling for cleaner PS1 output.

primary.why: Cool Boarders 3 is a PlayStation-only sequel with expanded characters, boards, and multiplayer, but it drops the previous game's System Link feature.
primary.how_to_play: Play on original PlayStation hardware or DuckStation with internal-resolution scaling.

emulation.notes: Use internal-resolution scaling for cleaner PS1 output.

primary.why: Cool Boarders 4 is a PlayStation-only entry with multiple tracks, characters, scenarios, and multiplayer; no other platform release is documented.
primary.how_to_play: Play on original PlayStation hardware or DuckStation with internal-resolution scaling.

emulation.notes: Use Dreamcast VGA/upscaled output for the cleanest route.

primary.why: This UEP Systems Dreamcast sequel is part of the Cool Boarders line under regional titles Cool Boarders Burrrn in Japan, Rippin' Riders in North America, and Snow Surfers in Europe; Dreamcast is the only sourced platform.
primary.how_to_play: Play on Dreamcast hardware or Flycast with VGA/upscaled output.

emulation.notes: Use original hardware or accurate NGPC emulation.

primary.version: Original Neo Geo Pocket Color release
primary.why: Cool Boarders Pocket is a Neo Geo Pocket Color-only isometric handheld spin-off; a planned US release was canceled after SNK USA closed its offices.
primary.how_to_play: Play on Neo Geo Pocket Color hardware or a compatible NGPC emulator.

entries.title: Cool Boarders 2001

emulation.notes: Use internal-resolution scaling for the PS2 version.

primary.why: Cool Boarders 2001 was released on PlayStation and later PlayStation 2 in North America; the PS2 version is the higher-fidelity route while preserving the same installment.
primary.how_to_play: Play the PlayStation 2 version on PS2 hardware or PCSX2 with internal-resolution scaling.

entries.remaster_caveats: PS2 port, not a modern remaster.

emulation.notes: Use internal-resolution scaling for the PS2 release.
